transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-10 15:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Liam Chen (Redwood CSM); Markus Voss (CTO - Zeppelin Ops), Ana Romero (Lead SRE), Taylor Brooks (Security), Priya Singh (PM)

Auto-summary (auto note):
- Kickoff and stakeholder handoff for Zeppelin Ops implementation of Redwood Inference.
- High-level network/VPC and security requirements captured; next steps: share network diagram, schedule private-deployment deep dive, provide sizing and pricing.
- Concerns: data residency, KMS/HSM integration, audit logs, latency SLOs for internal product.

Topics covered:
1) Scope and success criteria
2) Network & VPC peering
3) Security/compliance ask list (SOC2, key mgmt, audit logs)
4) Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private
5) Initial sizing, perf expectations, and pilot timeline
6) Next steps and owners

Transcript body:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. um quick roll call?
[00:06] Markus (Zeppelin): Markus here.
[00:07] Ana (Zeppelin): Ana here.
[00:09] Taylor: Taylor.
[00:11] Priya S: Priya (PM).
[00:13] Priya N (Redwood SE): Priya from Redwood. Liam?
[00:15] Liam (CSM): Here.
[00:18] Jordan: Great. So today the goal is kickoff — handoff from sales to CS/SE, capture infra constraints and security needs, and align on pilot timeline. We have about an hour.

[02:02] Jordan: Markus, can you give a 5 minute overview of the use case and the SLOs you're targeting for the pilot?
[02:12] Markus: Yeah sure. So we're building a real-time operational assistant for our internal incident triage — think chat + structured outputs. Target latency is sub-300ms tail for the short prompts, and throughput about 80-120 requests per minute during peak. We're sensitive to PII transit and want data not to be retained beyond processing (or to live in our VPC).

[04:05] Ana: From infra side, we prefer a private deployment but open to dedicated if we can't host on-prem. Our network team is strict re CIDRs and no inbound except peered endpoints. Also we have an on-prem HSM for key storage.

[05:32] Priya N (SE): Got it. Two quick clarifications — when you say sub-300ms tail, is that for first token or full generation?
[05:40] Markus: Good question. It's for the first token in the typical 30–60 token internal prompts. Full generation can be higher.

[06:10] Priya N: Okay that helps; that steers us toward a smaller context-optimized model and placement in the same region. Also we'll need your average sequence length distribution and concurrency patterns.

[07:01] Taylor (Security): On compliance — we need SOC2 artifacts, list of encryption at rest and in transit, and KMS integration details. If you support HSM we can map it to our key policies. Also audit logs per request are mandatory for our SOC auditors.

[08:10] Liam (CSM): We'll send the security pack, but to set expectations, Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and audit logging — there are a couple patterns for HSM integration we can walk through.

[09:00] Jordan: Quick note — for pilot speed we often recommend Redwood Dedicated to avoid lengthy network work, but I know you prefer private. Open to a phased approach: start dedicated to validate prompts/perf, then migrate to private/VPC for production. Thoughts?

[10:12] Ana: Phased approach makes sense but our security team may require the private option in the contract. We need to know the delta in ops and timelines.

[11:40] Priya N: Timeline wise, a Dedicated pilot can be up in 2–3 business days once you give us API access and a little traffic profile. Private typically takes 2–4 weeks depending on firewall and peering approvals — sometimes longer if HSM certs need exchange.

[13:05] Markus: What's the model onboarding flow look like? We want to pin model versions and lock quantization profiles to ensure deterministic results.

[13:30] Priya N: You can pin models; we support model versioning and rollout policies. For quantization, we can recommend 4-bit profiles but will validate quality with your evaluation prompts. We'll also run a few quality checks to detect regressions.

[15:00] Taylor: How do you handle KV cache and caching? We don't want stale context leaking across tenants — it's internal now but later might be multi-tenant.

[15:22] Priya N: By default we isolate KV cache per tenant and per session; for on-prem we can expose cache controls and TTLs. We'll include docs.

[17:10] Jordan: Pricing note — we'll provide a recommended Dedicated capacity profile (GPU type, instance count) based on your peak RPS and desired tail latency. That will have pricing ranges; moving to private can add infra + integration costs.

[18:00] Ana: Also network question — do you require inbound NAT or only VPC peering? Our firewall team prefers peering only.

[18:15] Priya N: We support VPC peering and private link patterns. The VPC peering checklist Jordan will share covers required routes and ports.

[20:05] Markus: On observability — we need token-level billing breakouts and per-route latency dashboards, plus trace-level sampling for a subset of calls.

[20:30] Liam: Redwood Console can show token-level cost and per-route latency, and we can configure tracing hooks for sampled requests. We'll attach example dashboards.

[22:00] Taylor: For auditability, we need immutable request logs. Is that possible with Private?

[22:12] Priya N: Yes, private mode can ship logs to your log collector or S3 with retention you control. We'll map the fields needed for audits.

[24:00] Jordan: Okay let's capture immediate blockers — network, KMS/HSM certs, and security artifact review. Anything else?
[24:12] Ana: One more — our incident ops want a playbook for graceful degradation: e.g., fallback to smaller model or cached answers if large model capacity is exhausted.

[24:30] Priya N: We have routing policies and automatic fallback to cheaper model variants; we can demo that in the SE deep-dive.

[26:40] Markus: For the pilot, we want a canary rollout to 5% traffic then 25% then broader. Also need a rollback plan.

[27:05] Priya N: That's standard — canary + A/B + automated fallback are supported. We'll capture rollout policy in the runbook.

[29:10] Jordan: Quick ops/design note — to size GPUs we need average tokens per request, average response length, and kv/cache hit rates. If you can share proxy traces or sample logs (sanitized) that helps compute costs.

[30:00] Ana: We'll sanitize and share a 24h sample by next Wednesday.

[31:35] Taylor: Any third-party vendor risk? We're evaluating Anthropic for certain workloads; want to compare reliability. Also curious if Redwood has any partner programs.

[31:50] Jordan: We can share benchmark summaries vs public models. Redwood focuses on serving economics and deterministic serving; we've seen lower tail latency in our internal tests versus some hosted alternatives. We'll include competitive notes.

[34:20] Priya N: On the private deployment, we need to coordinate with your network and security leads for a dedicated 60–90 minute technical session — we'll do deep-dive on peering, routing, HSM cert exchange, and observability endpoints.

[35:00] Ana: Let's schedule that — earliest Tuesday next week works for us.

[36:10] Jordan: Great. Liam I'll put a calendar invite and link to a preliminary agenda.

[37:40] Priya S (Customer PM): How are we measuring pilot success?
[37:45] Markus: Two main metrics: 1) 95th/99th percentile latency under our load, and 2) precision/recall of the structured outputs on our eval set (we'll share eval prompts). If both look good, we move to production pilot.

[39:10] Priya N: We'll run evals and produce a quality report and latency report. If regression occurs we'll explore quantization tweaks or model variant changes.

[41:00] Taylor: One last one — data residency: we need confirmation that logs and models will reside in our region only.

[41:12] Jordan: For private it's under your control; for dedicated/hosted we have region pinning and SLA clauses — we'll document exact boundaries. Liam will include region residency note in the packet.

[44:00] Markus: Can you also share a sample runbook for incident response around model downtime?

[44:10] Liam: Yes. We'll share runbook templates and a sample playbook that includes fallback routing, throttling, and customer notify steps.

[46:35] Jordan: Alright let's recap next steps and owners — (verbatim) Jordan will share VPC checklist and onboarding runbook; Priya (SE) will run sizing + perf calc; Ana to share sanitized traces and CIDRs; Taylor to send compliance list; Liam to drop security docs and invite for deep-dive.

[48:00] Markus: That sounds good. Any blockers from Redwood?

[48:05] Priya N: None immediate — just need the network artifacts. If you want to fast-track Dedicated pilot we can also spin up a test pool while the private process is underway.

[50:10] Ana: We'll discuss internally and confirm approach but appreciate the phased option.

[52:00] Jordan: Cool — we'll aim to have the security packet and pricing estimate in your inbox by next Tuesday. Deep-dive invite for the network/SE session will be sent today.

[54:30] Taylor: Minor transcribe note — we will want documentation on audit log schema; we'll review when you share.

[55:10] Jordan: Yep. Anything else before we close?
[55:20] Markus: No. Thanks, everyone.
[55:25] Ana: Thanks. Bye.
[55:28] Liam: Bye.

End of call.

Notes: some transcription artifacts present — speaker overlaps, occasional mis-heard acronyms (HSM sometimes transcribed as "H S M"), and informal language retained.
